proposals.announcement_evidence: pre-planned product improvement of the Joint Tactical Ground Station system
proposals.lexicon_quote: The Joint Tactical Ground Station (JTAGS) is a post-production, Acquisition Category (ACAT) III
proposals.rationale: The announcement spells the index name verbatim -- 'Joint Tactical Ground Station' -- and the work announced is pre-planned product improvement (P3I), i.e. development of the JTAGS system itself, not support to a platform that merely hosts it. Money colour agrees: the record states 'Fiscal 2015 research, development, testing, and evaluation funding for engineering services', and 0208053A is the Army RDT&E line whose own narrative (doc 359) describes JTAGS as 'a post-production, Acquisition Category (ACAT) III' program -- exactly the operational-systems-development posture a P3I action executes. The contracting activity, Army Space and Missile Defense Command, is JTAGS's own command. Within this org's index no other pe_bli owns the name; the only other JTAGS row in the lexicon is 1208053SF, a Space Force line that is not in A.tsv and is therefore out of scope for this proposal.

refute_a.reason: Money colour and mission both hold: FY2015 RDT&E dollars on an RDT&E operational-systems PE whose own index carries the project name 'Joint Tact Grd Station-P3I' for exactly the announced pre-planned product improvement, JTAGS is the program itself rather than a platform the contract supports, doc 359 is a single-program line not a rollup, and the 'engineering services' phrase describes the technical-directive funding mechanism on that named-system P3I contract, not a program-less services vehicle.

refute_b.reason: Name is real and exact in the index (A.tsv line 57) and 0208053A is its only owner in this org's index; the sole other JTAGS owner, 1208053SF (doc 417), is a Space Force line in F.tsv and out of scope, and the record's FY2015 Army RDT&E money and Army SMDC contracting activity point at the Army line, not the post-transfer Space Force one, with no variant/increment mismatch (P3I of a post-production ACAT III program is what this line funds).

proposals.rationale: The announcement names the end item and nothing else -- 'precision guidance kits' -- and the appropriation it names, 'procurement of ammunition, Army', is the appropriation 8750E27501 ('Artillery Propellants, Fuzes and Primers, All') is funded from, so this is a procurement action against a procurement line rather than O&M sustainment bolted onto one. Doc 349's narrative for this BLI defines PGK as its own subject: 'The Precision Guidance Kit (PGK) is a course correcting fuze that provides precision accurac[y]' -- PGK is a fuze, and this is the fuze line. On the collision lens B will find: 3102E89500 ('ARTILLERY PROJECTILE, 155MM, All Types') also carries the name, but its narrative mentions PGK only in a list of fuzes the projectile is used with ('...as well as Precision Guidance Kit (PGK)'), which is the section 3 'name is a thing the line merely supports' pattern read from the other side; the defining, owning narrative is this one. Northrop Grumman's Plymouth, Minnesota plant on W15QKN-13-C-0074 is the PGK production line, and the contracting activity is Picatinny/Newark, which buys Army ammunition.

refute_a.reason: Procurement money against a procurement line with no O&M-sustainment mismatch: 'Fiscal 2025 procurement of ammunition, Army' is the PAA appropriation this ammunition BLI is funded from, the kits are the end item bought rather than a platform merely supported, and doc 349's narrative for this BLI defines PGK as a course-correcting fuze, so a fuze buy is this line's own work; the title 'Artillery Propellants, Fuzes and Primers, All' is a multi-item ammunition BLI but not a catch-all (no threshold, 'Other' or 'Miscellaneous'), and the same-appropriation 3102E89500 collision is lens B's ground, not lens A's.

refute_b.reason: The name does collide three ways in A.tsv (0604802A doc 355, 3102E89500 doc 349, 8750E27501 doc 349), but the collisions resolve away from the alternatives rather than equally: the announcement's 'procurement of ammunition, Army' excludes the RDT&E Project S36 line, and 3102E89500's own lexicon quote lists PGK only among fuzes its 155mm projectile is used with, while the defining sentence 'The Precision Guidance Kit (PGK) is a course correcting fuze' sits on the proposed fuze line whose title is 'Artillery Propellants, Fuzes and Primers' -- and 'precision guidance kits' names the kit itself, not LR-PGK or any other variant, so the evidence is not a bare contractor name.

proposals.announcement_evidence: firm-fixed-price contract for new M1076A0 Palletized Load System trailers
proposals.lexicon_quote: Systems include the Heavy Expanded Mobility Tactical Truck (HEMTT) and the Palletized Load System (PLS).
proposals.rationale: The announcement names the index name verbatim -- 'Palletized Load System' -- as the system whose hardware is being bought, and the appropriation it names, 'Fiscal 2019 other procurement, Army funds', is the appropriation the Family of Heavy Tactical Vehicles BLI is funded from, so a new-build hardware buy is executing a procurement line with procurement money. Oshkosh Defense is the FHTV/PLS prime and the contracting activity is Detroit Arsenal, which owns tactical wheeled vehicles. The discriminator against the collision: the index carries PLS twice, here and at 8331D16506 ('PLS ESP'), whose narrative describes the Extended Service Program as a 'Recapitalization' effort -- recapitalising trucks already in service. The announcement says 'new M1076A0 ... trailers', which is new procurement, not recap, so the FHTV production line rather than the ESP line is the one whose own work this funds. The honest caveat for lens A to weigh: FHTV is a family line covering HEMTT as well as PLS, and the M1076 trailer is not itself named in either narrative row -- if lens A reads FHTV as a rollup, this does not survive, and that reading is defensible.

refute_a.reason: Appropriation agrees (FY2019 other procurement, Army on an OPA procurement BLI) and the action is new-build hardware, not O&M sustainment or recapitalisation; the trailer is PLS's own hardware rather than a separate platform the contract supports, and doc 346's FHTV narrative itself buys PLS trailers and their CTE/E-CHU kits as owned items while the 8331D16506 row records the ESP line being consolidated into DA0500 -- so PLS trailer procurement is this line's own work. FHTV is a named family program of record, not a catch-all (CATCHALL_TITLE does not match it and the loader does not exclude it); the family breadth plus the M1076 designator being absent from both narrative rows makes this the weakest of the four on the rollup ground, but not enough to break it on lens A's terms.

refute_b.reason: A different PE in the same index owns the name more strongly: 8331D16506 ('PLS ESP', doc 346) carries 'The Palletized Load System (PLS)' with the defining sentence 'is a 16.5-ton, 10-wheel drive truck', whereas the proposed 8309DA0500 row's own quote is family membership ('Systems include the Heavy Expanded Mobility Tactical Truck (HEMTT) and the Palletized Load System (PLS)'); the announcement offers only the bare name plus 'M1076A0', which appears in neither narrative, both PEs are 'other procurement, Army' so the money colour does not discriminate, and the new-build-vs-recap discriminator fails because 8309DA0500 itself also owns 'The PLS Extended Service Program (ESP)' (A.tsv line 1295) and a doc-346 row states the ESP program was consolidated into DA0500 -- so this evidence would link the award to 8331D16506 at least as well.

proposals.announcement_evidence: assist with technology transfer in the area of advanced lightweight polymer optics
proposals.lexicon_quote: Lightweight Polymers for Modern Small Caliber Apps - Ammo Casing Only
proposals.rationale: Rejected by design: the overlap is the material word 'lightweight polymer', and the index row scopes itself out of this award in its own title. The announcement buys technology transfer for 'advanced lightweight polymer optics'; the 0604115A row is 'Lightweight Polymers for Modern Small Caliber Apps - Ammo Casing Only', i.e. polymer cartridge cases for small-calibre ammunition, and the trailing 'Ammo Casing Only' is an explicit exclusion of everything else. Optics are not ammunition casings. Both sides happen to be RDT&E, Army, which is exactly why this pair is worth recording as refuted rather than left silent -- money colour alone would not have caught it.
